---
title: "Download & Project Setup"
description: |
  INTEGRATOR is a standalone executable and requires no installation. Download it, clear the
  one-time macOS or Windows security prompt, and retain one copy per analysis project so the
  project remains reproducible.
---

::: {.callout-important}
INTEGRATOR is not installed. It is a self-contained, portable executable: there is no installer,
and nothing is added to the system. It is downloaded, unzipped, and run from a folder.
:::

## One copy per project

The recommended approach is to keep one copy of the INTEGRATOR folder inside each data-analysis
project, alongside that project's raw data and input files. Because the executable, the parameters
(`param.txt`), the input files, and the results reside together in one self-contained folder, the
entire analysis remains reproducible: the folder can be re-opened months later, a parameter
adjusted, and the integration re-run exactly as before. Different projects can also use different
versions of INTEGRATOR without interfering with each other.

::: {.callout-note}
INTEGRATOR is not required to use the QUANT R package; QUANT imports directly from vendor outputs
(MassHunter, Skyline) as well. See the
[QUANT documentation ↗](https://slinghub.github.io/MRMhub/quant/).
:::

## Get the application

INTEGRATOR is distributed as pre-compiled executables for Windows and macOS, available from
<https://github.com/SLINGhub/MRMhub/releases>. Unzip the downloaded file and copy the folder into
the project location. The folder comprises the following files and subfolders: **MRMhub** is the
main application, and **MRMhub-viz** is an application for reviewing peak integration results.

## First launch (clear the security prompt)

The executable is unsigned, so the operating system displays a one-time security warning on first
launch. Clear it as follows.

On **macOS**, the following error is shown:

![](images/macOS_warning.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Screenshot of a macOS security dialog headed 'MRMhub Not Opened', warning that Apple could not verify the app is free of malware, with Done and Move to Bin buttons. This one-time block appears on first launch because the executable is unsigned."}

To resolve this, go to "**Systems Settings**", "**Privacy & Security**"
tab, and click "**Open Anyway**" button to enable the software.

![](images/security_setting.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Screenshot of the macOS System Settings Privacy and Security pane. Under Security, 'Allow applications from' reads App Store and Known Developers, and a row states that MRMhub was blocked to protect your Mac, beside an Open Anyway button that permits the app to run."}

On **Windows**, right-click on the executable, select
"**Properties**", and on the "**General**" tab, check the "**Unblock**"
box near the bottom if available, then click OK or Apply.

![](images/unblock.png){fig-align="center" fig-alt="Screenshot of the Windows MRMhub Properties dialog on the General tab. It identifies the file as an Application (.exe) of 1.33 MB and, near the bottom, shows a Security note that the file came from another computer and might be blocked, beside an Unblock checkbox that must be ticked to allow the app to run."}

## Folder layout

The input files required by the **MRMhub** application are
`feature_list.csv`, `run_order.csv`, and `param.txt`. The mzML folder is
used to store the mzML data files. All of these are explained in
[Input Files](input-files.qmd).
Furthermore, this distribution contains a test dataset, with a complete
set of input and raw data files, which can be used as templates for
future analysis. The `MRMhub_plot.r` is an R script used to generate the
PDFs. It can be modified to tailor for specific layouts and design
features of the plots.

![](images/paste-3.png){fig-align="center" width="526" fig-alt="Screenshot of a macOS Finder window for the MRMhub-INTEGRATOR project folder. It contains the _testdata and mzML folders, the MRMhub (1.4 MB) and MRMhub-viz (9.3 MB) executables, the MRMhub_plot.r plotting script, param.txt, README.txt, manual.pdf, and two input CSV files, feature_list.csv and run_order.csv."}
